subject: MMR
name: Myanmar
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. claims.title: Rise of the Pyu city-states
claims.summary: Tibeto-Burman Pyu peoples establish walled, moated cities such as Beikthano, Halin and Sri Ksetra in the Irrawaddy basin, founding the region's first urban civilization.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-200bce-rise-of-the-pyu-city-states, claim TL:MMR:event:200bce:rise-of-the-pyu-city-states, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Buddhism takes root
claims.summary: The Pyu cities provide the earliest evidence of Buddhism's introduction into Southeast Asia, embedding the religion in the region's culture and statecraft.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-200-buddhism-takes-root, claim TL:MMR:event:200:buddhism-takes-root, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decline of the Pyu
claims.summary: Raids from the Nanzhao kingdom and the southward migration of the Burman people erode Pyu power, clearing the way for the rise of Bagan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-832-decline-of-the-pyu, claim TL:MMR:event:832:decline-of-the-pyu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Bagan
claims.summary: The city of Bagan is traditionally established on a bend of the Irrawaddy, later to become the seat of the first Burmese kingdom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-849-founding-of-bagan, claim TL:MMR:event:849:founding-of-bagan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Anawrahta
claims.summary: Anawrahta unifies the Burman north and the Mon south into the first Burmese kingdom and adopts Theravada Buddhism as the state religion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1044-reign-of-anawrahta, claim TL:MMR:event:1044:reign-of-anawrahta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest of Thaton
claims.summary: Anawrahta captures the Mon city of Thaton, by tradition bringing Buddhist scriptures, monks and artisans that enrich Pagan's culture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1057-conquest-of-thaton, claim TL:MMR:event:1057:conquest-of-thaton, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mongol invasion and collapse
claims.summary: Armies of Kublai Khan's Mongol empire invade and shatter the kingdom; a further incursion in 1297 ends Bagan as a unifying power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1287-mongol-invasion-and-collapse, claim TL:MMR:event:1287:mongol-invasion-and-collapse, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Bayinnaung
claims.summary: Bayinnaung of the Toungoo dynasty reunifies Myanmar and conquers the Shan states and Siam, building the most powerful empire in mainland Southeast Asia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1551-reign-of-bayinnaung, claim TL:MMR:event:1551:reign-of-bayinnaung, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alaungpaya founds the Konbaung dynasty
claims.summary: The village chief Alaungpaya leads a revolt against Mon overlords and establishes the Konbaung dynasty, the last royal house of Burma.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1752-alaungpaya-founds-the-konbaung-dynasty, claim TL:MMR:event:1752:alaungpaya-founds-the-konbaung-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reconquest of Lower Burma
claims.summary: Alaungpaya's forces capture Pegu and subdue the Mon south, reuniting the country under Konbaung rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1757-reconquest-of-lower-burma, claim TL:MMR:event:1757:reconquest-of-lower-burma, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annexation of Arakan
claims.summary: Konbaung expansion absorbs the kingdom of Arakan on the western coast, bringing the Burmese frontier up against British-held Bengal.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1784-annexation-of-arakan, claim TL:MMR:event:1784:annexation-of-arakan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Anglo-Burmese War
claims.summary: War over the Arakan and Assam frontiers ends with the Treaty of Yandabo (1826), forcing Burma to cede Arakan and Tenasserim to Britain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1824-first-anglo-burmese-war, claim TL:MMR:event:1824:first-anglo-burmese-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Anglo-Burmese War
claims.summary: British forces annex Lower Burma, including the Irrawaddy delta and the province renamed Pegu, tightening control of the coastline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1852-second-anglo-burmese-war, claim TL:MMR:event:1852:second-anglo-burmese-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Third Anglo-Burmese War and the end of the monarchy
claims.summary: Britain takes Mandalay, exiles King Thibaw, and annexes Upper Burma on 1 January 1886, abolishing the Burmese monarchy and completing the conquest.

sources.label: History of Myanmar: The British in Burma, 1885-1948

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1885-third-anglo-burmese-war-and-the-end-of-the, claim TL:MMR:event:1885:third-anglo-burmese-war-and-the-end-of-the, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Burma separated from British India
claims.summary: Burma is made a distinct crown colony with limited self-government, administered separately from the Indian Empire.

sources.label: History of Myanmar: The British in Burma, 1885-1948

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1937-burma-separated-from-british-india, claim TL:MMR:event:1937:burma-separated-from-british-india, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Aung San
claims.summary: Aung San, who had negotiated independence with Britain, is assassinated with most of his cabinet months before the transfer of power.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Burma
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1947-assassination-of-aung-san, claim TL:MMR:event:1947:assassination-of-aung-san, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of the Union of Burma
claims.summary: Burma becomes a fully independent republic outside the Commonwealth under Prime Minister U Nu, soon facing communist and ethnic insurgencies.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Burma
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1948-independence-of-the-union-of-burma, claim TL:MMR:event:1948:independence-of-the-union-of-burma, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ne Win's coup
claims.summary: General Ne Win overthrows the elected government, imprisons U Nu, and inaugurates decades of military rule under the Burmese Way to Socialism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1962-ne-win-s-coup, claim TL:MMR:event:1962:ne-win-s-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 8888 uprising
claims.summary: A nationwide pro-democracy uprising is crushed by the military, which forms a new junta; Aung San Suu Kyi emerges as the democracy movement's leader.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1988-the-8888-uprising, claim TL:MMR:event:1988:the-8888-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annulled NLD election victory
claims.summary: Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy wins elections in a landslide, but the junta ignores the result and detains her for years.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-1990-annulled-nld-election-victory, claim TL:MMR:event:1990:annulled-nld-election-victory, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Saffron Revolution
claims.summary: Buddhist monks lead mass protests against the regime that are violently suppressed, drawing renewed international condemnation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-2007-the-saffron-revolution, claim TL:MMR:event:2007:the-saffron-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reforms under Thein Sein
claims.summary: A quasi-civilian government begins political and economic liberalization, releasing prisoners, easing censorship, and restoring Aung San Suu Kyi's freedoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-2011-reforms-under-thein-sein, claim TL:MMR:event:2011:reforms-under-thein-sein, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: NLD wins free elections
claims.summary: Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy wins Myanmar's first fairly contested elections; she becomes state counsellor in a government sharing power with the army.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-2015-nld-wins-free-elections, claim TL:MMR:event:2015:nld-wins-free-elections, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rohingya crisis in Rakhine State
claims.summary: Military 'clearance operations' drive more than 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh; a UN fact-finding mission later finds evidence of genocidal violence.

sources.label: UN Fact-Finding Mission on Myanmar: account of violations in Rakhine, Kachin and Shan States
sources.publisher: United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR)

claims.title: Military coup
claims.summary: The army seizes power, detains Aung San Suu Kyi and the elected leadership, and installs a junta under Min Aung Hlaing, triggering mass protests and civil war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Myanmar: From the Buddhist city-states of the Irrawaddy and the temple-strewn plain of Bagan to a modern nation forged by empire, war, and a long contest between army and democracy.", terralore.co/country/MMR/chronicle#ev-2021-military-coup, claim TL:MMR:event:2021:military-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
